name: Legal Studies
notes: Six courses. An interdisciplinary minor administered by the philosophy department that examines law from several perspectives. It is NOT pre-professional training, though it should be useful for anyone considering law school.

DIVISION IS YOUR CHOICE: to count as a HUMANITIES minor you must take at least three humanities courses (all English and philosophy courses except PHIL 110); to count as a SOCIAL SCIENCES minor, at least three social-science courses (anthropology, economics, history, political science and sociology). Filed here under humanities; the planner does not count the split, and the page marks each course (H) or (S).
No more than two courses used for your major(s) may be used toward the minor.
Work with a legal studies minor advisor (Professors Terlazzo in philosophy, Flores in history, or Johnson in political science) to create a course plan before declaring.
CASC 304 was valid only until spring 2021 and the older LAW 205 listing only until spring 2019.

requirementGroups.label: Two analytical technique courses
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Analytical Techniques: ECON/PSCI 288: Game Theory (S); ENGL 135: Debate (H); ENGL 280: Advanced Debate (H); PHIL 105: Reason and Argument (H); PHIL 110: Introductory Logic; PSCI 107: Introduction to Positive Political Theory (S); PSCI 202: Argument in Political Science (S); PSCI 281: Formal Models in Political Sciences (S)

requirementGroups.label: One legal studies course
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Legal Studies (at least one required): ANTH 230: Post-Conflict Justice (S); ANTH 231: (IL)Legal Anthropology (S); ANTH 233: Cultural Politics of Prison Towns (S); CASC 304: Urban Crime and Justice (valid until spring 2021); EDU 490: Higher Education Law; LAW 205: Business Law: Contracts and Legal Entities; PHLT/PSCI 230: Public Health Law and Policy (S); PHLT/PSCI 236: Health Care and the Law (S); PHIL 223: Social and Political Philosophy (H); PHIL 226: Philosophy of Law (H); PSCI 212: Supreme Court in US History (S); PSCI 214: Race and Law (S); PSCI 223: Constitutional Structures and Rights (S); PSCI 234: Law and Politics in the United States (S); PSCI 239/INTR 239: International Environmental Law (S); PSCI 240: Criminal Procedures and Constitutional Principles (S); PSCI 242: Research Practicum in Criminal Justice Reform (S); PSCI 246: Environmental Law and Policy (S); PSCI 291: First Amendment and Religion (S); RELC 182: Religion and Law (H); RELC 183: Incarceration Nation (H)

requirementGroups.label: One cognate course
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Cognate Courses (at least one required): ANTH 104; ANTH 202; ANTH 205; CASC 152; ECON 220; ENGL 286; HIST 164; HIST 166; HIST 228; HIST 260; HIST 261; HIST 269; HIST 362W; PHIL 103; PHIL 225; PHIL 230; PSCI 209; PSCI 215; PSCI 218; PSCI 255; PSCI 263; PSCI 284; PSCI 287; PSCI 291; RELC 226/FMST 265: Guilt (H)

requirementGroups.label: Two further courses from any category
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Students must take a total of six courses from the lists below, with at least: Two analytical technique courses; One legal studies course; One cognate course. The remaining two required courses can come from any category.
